hints.title: Collision Invariance
hints.text: When identical robots collide and reverse directions, the set of positions behaves as if they simply passed through one another.

hints.title: Independent Trajectories
hints.text: Compute the independent final position of each robot after d seconds.

hints.title: Sorted Pairwise Distances
hints.text: Sort the final positions and calculate the sum of pairwise distances using the contribution of each element based on its index.

hints.title: Mathematical Distance Summation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def sumDistance(self, nums: list[int], s: str, d: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums)
        pos = []
        for i in range(n):
            delta = d if s[i] == 'R' else -d
            pos.append(nums[i] + delta)
        pos.sort()
        total = 0
        for i in range(n):
            term = pos[i] * (2 * i - n + 1)
            total = (total + term) % MOD
        return (total % MOD + MOD) % MOD
```

complexity.notes: Sorting determines positions on the 1D line to compute all pairwise distances in O(n).
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating collisions second-by-second takes O(d * n) time where d can be 10^9.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Linear storage holds final positions before sorting.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes collision equivalence and computes pairwise distances linearly.
